by: stand-in planner (replan 2026-11-09): verified claims kept word for word

checks.claim: A family septic tank often holds around 1,000 gallons, the usual minimum for a three-bedroom home.
checks.why: The encyclopedia gives an average of 1,000 gallons and sizing guides call 1,000 gallons the common minimum for 3 bedrooms; codes vary and some say 1,250, so 'often around' fits.

checks.claim: In a septic tank solids settle to the bottom as sludge while fats, oil and grease float to the top as scum
checks.why: EPA and LA County Public Health describe exactly these three layers.

sources.title: How Your Septic System Works - US EPA
How a Septic System Works - LA County Public Health

checks.claim: A household septic tank is typically pumped every 3 to 5 years
checks.why: Cornell's copy of the EPA homeowner guide says sludge and scum should generally be pumped every three to five years.

sources.title: Your Septic System - Cornell Cooperative Extension
